extracted.intended_audience: registrants, accountants, auditors, and securities lawyers preparing SEC filings for real estate acquisitions (including REITs)
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretive guidance on applying S-X Rule 3-14 (real estate operations) to determine significance of acquisitions/dispositions and the related financial statement and pro forma filing requirements, including special rules for REITs, blind-pool offerings, newly formed REIT IPOs, and aggregation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: 20% significance threshold for real estate operations
rubrics_metrics.description: For acquisitions or dispositions that are real estate operations as defined in §210.3-14(a)(2), substitute 20 percent for 10 percent each place the significance threshold appears (i.e., the investment-test threshold is 20%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S-X Rule 3-14 modifies the significant subsidiary/investment test for real estate operations so the 20% threshold is used instead of the usual 10% in the specified rules; if significance exceeds 20% then required financial statements and supplemental information must be filed as specified by S-X Rule 3-14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of amounts for significance determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination of significance must generally be made using the registrant's most recent annual consolidated financial statements required to be filed at or prior to the date of acquisition or disposition and the business's pre-acquisition/pre-disposition financial statements for the same fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fiscal years differ, use the business's most recent fiscal year that would be required if it had the same filer status as the registrant. The rule allows specified alternatives (see next item) and requires application of §210.11-01(b)(3)/(4) when determining periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted alternatives for amounts used in significance tests (A/B/C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternatives to the primary financial statements include: (A) financial statements permitted by §210.3-05(e) or (f) if eligible; (B) pro forma amounts for the registrant for the applicable periods that only depict significant acquisitions/dispositions consummated after the latest fiscal year-end and include only Transaction Accounting Adjustments; or (C) the registrant's annual consolidated financial statements included in a Form 10-K filed after the acquisition/disposition but before the date financials/pro forma would be required on Form 8-K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For (B) conditions: registrant must have filed audited financial statements for any such acquired business for the periods required by §210.3-05 or §210.3-14 and the pro forma information required by Articles 11; tests may not be made by 'annualizing' data; if pro forma amounts are used to determine significance, the registrant must continue to use pro forma amounts until the filing date of its next Form 10-K or Form 20-F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related businesses: combine pre-acquisition financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the business is a related business (see §210.3-05(a)(3)), use combined pre-acquisition financial statements of the group of related businesses for the fiscal year specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the combined presentation rules where the acquired businesses are related as defined in the rules; see §210.3-05 guidance for related-business aggregation mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous-offering (blind-pool) adjustments to tests
rubrics_metrics.description: When a registrant conducts a continuous offering over an extended period and applies Industry Guide 5 Item 20.D undertakings (blind pool), the income test does not apply; determination is made using the investment test (and asset test if applicable) with modified measures of total assets during and after the distribution period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the distribution period include total assets as of date of acquisition plus proceeds (net of commissions) in good faith expected to be raised in the registered offering over the next 12 months (excluding the acquired business for acquisitions). After the distribution period until the next Form 10-K, use total assets as of acquisition date (excluding acquired business for acquisitions). After that next Form 10-K, follow standard guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro forma effects presentation exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Pro forma effects of a business acquisition need not be presented if separate financial statements of the acquired business are not included in the filing, except where the aggregate impact of acquired or probable-to-be-acquired businesses is significant as determined by applicable rules (e.g., §210.3-05(b)(2)(iv) or §210.3-14(b)(2)(i)(C)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where aggregate significance thresholds are met, pro forma financial information depicting the aggregate impact and sometimes separate audited financial statements will be required despite the absence of separate historical statements in other cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment test is the primary/sole test for real estate operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Real estate operations are evaluated for significance using the investment test (as modified under S-X Rule 3-14); the investment test is calculated as investments in and advances to the acquired business divided by the registrant's AWMV, if available, otherwise registrant's consolidated total assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AWMV (aggregate worldwide market value) is preferred because purchase price approximates fair value; if AWMV is available, calculate the investment test as discussed in section 3.4. If AWMV is not available, use consolidated total assets and apply S-X Rule 3-14 modifications (see next criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment-test modification when AWMV unavailable (include assumed debt)
rubrics_metrics.description: When registrant does not have AWMV (e.g., non-traded REIT or IPO), use consolidated total assets as denominator and modify the numerator to include any debt secured by the real properties that is assumed by the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerator = investments in and advances to the acquired business + any assumed debt secured by the real properties; denominator = registrant's consolidated total assets. This modification recognizes the common structure of real estate acquisitions where assumed mortgage debt reduces cash paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance >20% requires S-X 3-14 financial statements and supplemental info
rubrics_metrics.description: If significance exceeds 20% for an acquired real estate operation, financial statements are required for the periods indicated by S-X Rule 3-14, including supplemental information required by S-X Rule 3-14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the periods-to-be-presented rules in S-X Rule 3-14 and include specified supplemental disclosures (section 8.4 outlines the filing and reporting requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of performing the significance test
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant performs the significance test once it determines an acquisition is in the scope of S-X Rule 3-14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This timing is aligned with S-X Rule 3-05 requirements and means the test is performed at the point the acquisition falls under S-X Rule 3-14 scope (see chapter 2 and section 8.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Information periods used in the significance test
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance is determined based on information of the registrant and the acquired business or real estate operation from the financial statements of the most recently completed fiscal year (subject to the period selection rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If registrant is conducting a continuous offering (blind pool) special considerations apply (S-X Rule 11-01(b)(4)); see section 8.5.10 for blind-pool specifics. Use §210.11-01(b)(3)/(4) when determining periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anomalous results: apply tests as written but may seek relief under S-X Rule 3-13
rubrics_metrics.description: If the investment test produces an anomalous result due to capital structure (e.g., AWMV much less than total assets), the tests must be applied as written, but registrants may seek relief under S-X Rule 3-13 if they consider the results anomalous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC staff has commented anomalous results are not unique to S-X Rule 3-14; administrative relief (rule 3-13) may be pursued where appropriate (see section 10.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation of individually insignificant acquisitions for registration/proxy statements
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant must consider the aggregate impact of individually insignificant acquisitions (categories: consummated <20%; acquisitions between 20% and 50% but within 75‑day grace; probable acquisitions <50%) since the most recent audited balance sheet; if aggregate impact exceeds 50% under the investment test, the registrant must provide pro forma financial information and, for any acquired or probable acquisition >20% significant, financial statements covering the most recent fiscal year and interim period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aggregation requirement applies to registration statements and certain proxy materials; it ensures that multiple individually small acquisitions that are material in the aggregate trigger pro forma and historical reporting requirements under S-X Rule 3-14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different aggregation rules for Form 8-K vs registration/proxy
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregating individually insignificant acquisitions for the 50% test is required only for registration statements and certain proxy materials; Form 8-K requires aggregating individually insignificant acquisitions only if they are related businesses and are, in the aggregate, significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the narrower Form 8-K aggregation standard (related businesses + aggregate significance) when determining whether to file separate financial statements on Form 8-K within the 75-day grace period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for mixed S-X Rule 3-05 and S-X Rule 3-14 acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: When some acquisitions are in scope of S-X Rule 3-05 and others in scope of S-X Rule 3-14, determine significance by: (Step 1) determining individual significance per applicable rule; (Step 2) determine which acquisitions meet aggregation criteria (less than 20% or 20–50% but not yet consummated or within 75-day grace); (Step 3) aggregate financial data used in Step 1 (include both businesses and real estate operations for investment test; aggregate income and asset tests only include businesses in scope of 3-05); (Step 4) if aggregate exceeds 50% for any test, provide pro forma and required financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If aggregate exceeds 50% significance, the registrant must include pro forma financial information and audited financial statements for any acquired or probable acquisition >20% as required by the applicable rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified denominator for newly formed REIT IPOs
rubrics_metrics.description: For a newly formed REIT with no significant operations, the SEC staff permits using a denominator equal to the total cost of: properties acquired immediately prior to filing the initial registration statement; properties to be acquired upon closing the IPO; and properties identified as probable future acquisitions, in lieu of registrant AWMV or total assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significance is determined the same otherwise, and the registrant applies S-X Rule 3-14 financial statement requirements using the substituted denominator; the denominator should be reduced for properties no longer probable or not acquired when used for subsequent post-filing acquisitions until the first Form 10‑K is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission and filing timing for recently consummated acquisitions (74/75-day rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration statements not subject to §230.419 and proxy statements need not include separate financial statements of an acquired real estate operation if neither the operation nor the aggregate impact exceeds the significance condition at 50% and either (A) the consummation has not occurred, or (B) the final prospectus/proxy mailing date is no more than 74 days after consummation and financial statements have not previously been filed; omitted financial statements must be filed under Form 8-K no later than 75 days after consummation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the 75-day grace-period regime: if financials are omitted under the grace rule, registrant (other than certain foreign private issuers) must file the omitted financials and any required pro forma information on Form 8-K within 75 days of consummation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission of separate financial statements after consolidated results reflected for nine months
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate financial statements of the acquired real estate operation need not be presented once the operating results of the acquired real estate operation have been reflected in the audited consolidated financial statements of the registrant for at least nine months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule avoids duplication when the acquired operation's results are already incorporated sufficiently in the registrant's audited consolidated statements.
